title: Meta threat alert, relayed through the FBI, brings Paraguayan police and psychologists to a bullied 17-year-old who praised the Uvalde shooter
summary: Meta's platform flagged a Paraguayan teenager's post praising the Uvalde shooter, and after the FBI relayed the alert, police, prosecutors and psychologists visited him.
account: On Thursday 26 May 2022, two days after the Uvalde school shooting, Paraguay's Policía Nacional and Ministerio Público received an alert. It came from Meta's platform and the FBI office in Buenos Aires. A user in Paraguay had tagged the shooter, called himself his “fan” and said something similar could happen in Paraguay with more victims. Comisario Diosnel Alarcón's cybercrime department identified the Instagram profile as a 17-year-old in the “zona central”. He lived with a relative and was treated as a bullying victim. Police, prosecutors, the children's defender and psychologists visited the home and recommended urgent psychological support, and also visited a friend who knew of the posts. No weapon or plan was reported.
purpose: Meta's content-detection and law-enforcement referral process exists to find posts that threaten violence or self-harm. It passes credible threats to the authorities of the user's country. Flagging this post and alerting the police was that purpose.
system: Meta (Facebook/Instagram) violence-threat detection and law-enforcement referral process
domain: Online safety and threat referral to law enforcement
taxonomy_note: A threat of a copycat shooting was checked and the minor given psychological support, but no weapon or plan was found and the detection is not shown to be automated.

ratings.reason: Prosecutors' psychologists visited the 17-year-old and recommended urgent psychological support. No source reports that he received that support or any other outcome from the visit.
Officials checked the public statement within a day, and no weapon or plan was found. Police said that many such alerts prove to be jokes, so no prevented harm is established.

ai_role.statement: Officials said the network detected the comment, classified it as dangerous and reported it. It went to the FBI and a 24/7 channel shared by prosecutors and the cybercrime police. Alarcón also spoke of corroborating “datos de analítica artificial” before the visit. No source says the flag was automated. Meta documents that its technology proactively detects most violating content before anyone reports it, but its referrals to law enforcement also pass through human review. Identifying the user, the home visit and the psychological support were the work of Paraguayan police, prosecutors and the child-protection office.

display.answer: The six news reports quote Paraguayan police and prosecutors, chiefly the cybercrime official Diosnel Alarcón. The EFE agency report appears through Vanguardia. Meta's own page describes its detection in general terms and says nothing about this case.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: Meta's platform flagged a Paraguayan teenager's post praising the Uvalde shooter, and after the FBI relayed the alert, police, prosecutors and psychologists visited him.
fields.account: On Thursday 26 May 2022, two days after the Uvalde school shooting, Paraguay's Policía Nacional and Ministerio Público received an alert. It came from Meta's platform and the FBI office in Buenos Aires. A user in Paraguay had tagged the shooter, called himself his “fan” and said something similar could happen in Paraguay with more victims. Comisario Diosnel Alarcón's cybercrime department identified the Instagram profile as a 17-year-old in the “zona central”. He lived with a relative and was treated as a bullying victim. Police, prosecutors, the children's defender and psychologists visited the home and recommended urgent psychological support, and also visited a friend who knew of the posts. No weapon or plan was reported.

provenance.basis: Última Hora’s May 28, 2022 interview with the police cybercrime official.

produced_by: A platform practice of reporting threats of violence to law enforcement in the user's country. Here, via the FBI's Buenos Aires office and a 24/7 police-prosecutor channel.
A cybercrime unit able to identify an account holder from the platform's primary data within hours
A welfare rather than punitive response, with prosecutors, the children's defender and psychologists attending
must_hold: The referral must carry enough account data to identify a real person; police said many flagged profiles are fake or jokes
The response must stay proportionate for a minor; the Monitor flags rights, psychological and reputational risks to the child
The platform's detection and referral thresholds, which are not public for this case, must stay in place for the alert to recur

echoes.setting: Quilmes, Buenos Aires province, Argentina: the FBI legal attaché at the U.S. embassy alerted Argentine federal police to a 15-year-old who reportedly used ChatGPT to plan a school attack, and police searched his home. The report does not say who first detected the conversations.
